instrumentation_comparison.scope: same actual D2 binary, enabled versus disabled only; disabled hooks versus production A23 not measured

interpretation_limits: This compares diagnostic-on versus diagnostic-off within the same actual D2 binary. Disabled-hook cost versus production A23 was not measured.

The two temporal pairs reverse direction for CPU, goodput and p95. Tolerance gates pass, but this is a descriptive short calibration, not a precise stable overhead estimate or proof of zero perturbation.
Owner-thread lifetime shares include initialization, preflight or restart readbacks, background activity and shutdown. They do not allocate timed-cell or whole-controller CPU.
read_and_hash combines reads, buffer handling and digest updates; digest finalization belongs to after_stamps_and_digest. Pure SHA cost is not isolated.
Agent wall intervals overlap. Their sums are not additive elapsed time and do not measure CPU, master renewals or remote-agent causality.
First and restart owner lifetimes are separately retained and aggregated. Shutdown references are not extra diagnostic samples.
There were no spawn-proof failure events in this short calibration. This does not explain or retroactively clear the earlier r01 identity failure.
All 17 sampling errors are retained. RSS/FD/tree peaks are 100 ms lifetime sampled lower bounds; no stable level, time series or per-phase CPU allocation is claimed.
Complete diagnostic records never rescue failed native calls or missing evidence; the frozen quality gate still applies.
The plan reports one continuous forwarded-agent session and no compilation overlap; report timestamps confirm serial order, not every external host activity.
No A24 qualification, runtime fault fix, physical power-loss recovery or exhaustive-optimization conclusion is established by this D2 calibration.
